newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aramco naphtha bid at double-digit premium - traders.
newsitem.headline: Aramco naphtha bid at double-digit premium - traders.

text.p: Term naphtha buyers in Japan and South Korea were believed to have bid double-digit premiums for Saudi Arabia's A-180 naphtha in the first round of bidding that closed last Friday, traders said on Monday.
Trading houses and petrochemical firms in East Asia were likely to have bid at $11 to $14 per tonne over the Aramco formula for A-180 cargoes to be lifted in the second half of 1997, they said.

While bidding levels were widely scattered, most potential buyers were believed to have submitted bids with a premium of $11 or $12, compared with a $6.50 premium for the first half of the year, they said.
The bids are valid until May 21.
Saudi Aramco is expected to invite potential buyers for face-to-face negotiations before the bids expire, they said.
Asian buyers import about 4.5 million tonnes of term naphtha per year from Saudi Arabia, they added.
